due_when.clears_when: the writer that holds trade_journal.db's write lock for >3 s during a burst is named from a measurement, and either fixed (no burst over a 48 h complete journalctl scan) or killed with a stated reason

origin.rerun: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh 'journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live&since=<24h ago>&lines=200&grep=database%20is%20locked' (or the vm-diag-request relay with that path); count lines and bursts

what: Identify the holder of the trade_journal.db write lock behind the recurring 'database is locked' bursts on the live trader. MEASURED 2026-11-05 (journalctl via diag relay #23192/#23193, 2026-11-04T00:00Z to 2026-11-05T08:12Z): 59 lines in ~16 bursts of 10 s to 2 min; 55 are signal_audit_logger dual-write failures (a waiter, 3 s busy timeout), 4 are the 02:20Z order_monitor burst. The 08:00:30-08:01:12Z burst stretched an exit pass to 42.0 s and breached EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL (71.2 s). PR for TICK-STAGE2-RECONCILE-OFFTICK bounds the exit thread's exposure (0.25 s telemetry write timeout), but the holder is not known: the relay cannot see sqlite lock owners. Ruled out: ml_decision_shadow (no journal write), db_integrity (mode=ro). Next step: instrument write-transaction hold time in src.units.db.database.Database and the long-lived writers (thread + caller name when a commit follows >1 s after BEGIN), or sample /proc/<pid>/fd + journalctl at a burst via a system-action. | [2026-11-05 lane ML-ENTRY-WATCHDOG-EXIT] SECOND INSTANCE, MEASURED (journalctl via diag_fetch, 16:56:10-16:57:35Z, read_state complete, 463 lines): 'database is locked' on _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade 16:56:49, venue_protection_snapshot 16:57:01, position_path_history 16:57:07, order_monitor protective-level sync + order_packages update 16:57:21/24, signal_audit_logger 16:57:29. The exit-loop's per-pass order_monitor lines gapped 16:56:15 -> 16:57:29 (74.0 s), which is the 16:58Z 'EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL BREACHED 74.3s' page (process started 16:51:10, so NOT the restart). Holder still unknown. | [2026-11-05 lane MECH-FOLLOWUPS-1105, for Manager 2026-11-05b] TREND EVIDENCE, exit-eval interval vs its 60 s requirement (numbers as reported by the manager's routine; the 16:58Z page is the one already recorded above): 74.3 s BREACH at 16:58Z (attributed above to the 16:56:49-16:57:29Z lock burst); 56.5 s near miss at 20:01Z; 59.0 s near miss at 21:47Z. Three crossings above 56 s in ~5 h, so this is a trend, not a one-off. CHEAP DIAG READ (journalctl via diag_fetch, read_state complete, both windows scanned fully, grep=locked|EXIT-EVAL|slow|timeout|retry): 21:47Z (21:45:30-21:48:30, 1562 lines, 14 matched): SAME SIGNATURE as 16:57Z — 'database is locked' x5 between 21:47:09 and 21:47:25 (signal_audit_logger dual-write x3, _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade at 21:47:18), and the order_monitor GLD lines are 59 s apart across it (21:46:17 -> 21:47:16), matching the 59.0 s figure. 20:01Z (20:00:00-20:02:30, 592 lines, 10 matched): NO 'database is locked' line in the window, so the 56.5 s near miss is NOT explained by the lock; in that window the tick was serially retrying per-strategy 1h bars from the venue (spy/qqq/tlt/slv/uso_pullback/trend_1h, 'venue has not published this session's 1h bar yet', 6-12 s apart, 20:00:16-20:00:51) right at the hour boundary. HYPOTHESIS ONLY (not established; whether the exit pass shares a thread/resources with that fetch was not checked): broker/venue bar reads at the :00 boundary. Also: the trader PID differs between the two windows (2227932 at 20:01, 2285115 at 21:47), i.e. a restart happened in between. NOT MEASURED: the per-pass exit-eval duration itself (no per-phase timing is logged), the lock holder, and which of the two causes (DB lock vs venue reads) dominates over a full day. SUGGESTED OWNER: the TICK-STAGE2-RECONCILE-OFFTICK lane (it already bounds the exit thread's telemetry write at 0.25 s and owns the exit-loop timing); the lock-holder instrumentation named in Next step above is the way to settle the DB half, and a per-phase timer in the exit pass (DB / broker read / strategy monitor) settles which half dominates.
